QF.id: SIA Social Impact Assessment and Assessors_34

question.text: Under Section 5.11.2, materiality in SIA should be determined by:

answer.text: A fixed INR threshold applied uniformly across all engagements
Quantitative factors only — qualitative factors are excluded under SAS
The context of both quantitative AND qualitative factors, considering their effect on the evaluation of the subject matter
The SE's own materiality policy without independent SIA judgement

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 5.11.2 states: 'Materiality should consider the context of quantitative and qualitative factors and the effect of these factors on the evaluation of the subject matter.' Materiality in SIA is context-specific and blends both dimensions — not a fixed rupee threshold. The Trap: A wrongly imposes a uniform INR rule. B wrongly excludes qualitative factors — a bread-and-butter distractor. D violates independence by deferring wholly to the SE. Cross-Exam Context: NISM XV (RA) and financial audit materiality frameworks also combine quantitative + qualitative; XXIII is closer to the qualitative end because social outcomes are harder to monetise. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Document your materiality threshold and reasoning at the planning stage and keep it fixed for the engagement duration — movement in materiality during fieldwork to accommodate findings is a frequent ICAI SIAB disciplinary touchpoint.
